s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging facial swelling with bony destruction
salient_findings: Diffuse, firm, non-tender mass on the left cheek
Vestibular swelling extending from the distal aspect of the left canine to the second molar
Bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old South Asian man
3-month history of gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek
Mass measures about 4 × 5 cm
Mass extends from the infraorbital region to the lip commissure
Mass obliterates the nasal ala medially and approaches the preauricular area laterally
Intraoral examination reveals a well-defined vestibular swelling
Vestibular swelling measures 4 × 3 cm
Routine hematologic parameters are within normal limits
Contrast-enhanced CT shows a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion
Incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common malignancy of the head and neck region

shortlist.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Salivary gland malignancy that can present as a facial swelling

shortlist.label: Lymphoma of the maxilla
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause destructive lesions of the facial bones

shortlist.label: Ameloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign but locally aggressive tumor of the jaw

shortlist.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Known for its potential to cause bony destruction

shortlist.label: Giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause facial swelling and bony destruction

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Benign condition that can cause facial asymmetry and swelling

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant bone tumor that can present with facial swelling and bony destruction

raw.rationale: The incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, which is more consistent with lymphoma, and the clinical presentation of a rapidly enlarging mass in the maxilla is also consistent with lymphoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not indicate a salivary gland tumor

rejected.label: Ameloblastoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a slow-growing, painless swelling, which does not match the rapid growth described

rejected.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents with a well-defined radiolucency, which is not described in the CT findings

rejected.label: Giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more localized lesion and does not match the extensive involvement described

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Does not typically present with a rapidly enlarging mass

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not indicate a primary bone malignancy
